question: Who introduced binomial nomenclature?
solution:
The correct option is __**Carolus Linnaeus.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

EXPLANATION:

Carolus Linnaeus:

__
 
• **Carolus Linnaeus **is best known for Scientific classification and** Binomial nomenclature.**
 
• He is also known as the **father of modern taxonomy.**
 
• He is also known by the name** Carl von Linne.**
 
• He created a new system of classification for all living things.
 
• This nomenclature system was given by him in his book '**Species Plantarum'.**
 
• In this technique, any living organism is named in two parts.
 
• **For example** - the fruit mango is called "Mangifera indica",
 
• In this '**Magnifera'** is the name showing its **genus** while **'indica'** shows the **script.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Dmitri Mendeleev:**

 
• The** Periodic table is discovered by Dmitri Mendeleev.**
 
• Dmitri Mendeleev laid the foundation of the modern periodic table.
 
• He organized elements into groups and rows according to their physical and chemical behavior.
 
• Mendeleev arranged elements based on their atomic mass and physical properties.
 
• Mendeleev also predicted some properties of unidentified elements that were expected to fill gaps within the table. 

**John Dalton:**

 
• In 1808, **John Dalton first proposed an atomic theory of matter and he named it Dalton's atomic theory.**
 
• Dalton’s atomic theory was able to explain the law of conservation of mass, the law of constant composition, and the law of multiple proportions very successfully
 
• As per the theory, all matter whether it is a mixture, compound, or element, consists of invisible particles called ‘atoms’. 

**Claude Louis Berthollet:**

 
• Claude Louis Berthollet was a **Savoyard-French chemist.**
 
• He is known for his **scientific contributions to the theory of chemical equilibria via the mechanism of reverse chemical reactions.**
 
• He was the** first to demonstrate the bleaching action of chlorine gas.**
 
• He was the** first to develop a solution of sodium hypochlorite as a modern bleaching agent.**
